solution:
Given \(xy = \log y + c\).

Differentiate both sides with respect to \(x\):

\(\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(\log y + c)\)

\(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = \dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

Multiply throughout and collect the \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) terms:

\(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{y}\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -y\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\left(x - \dfrac{1}{y}\right) = -y\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\left(\dfrac{xy - 1}{y}\right) = -y\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{-y \cdot y}{xy - 1} = \dfrac{-y^2}{xy - 1} = \dfrac{y^2}{1 - xy}\)

This is exactly the given differential equation, so \(xy = \log y + c\) is a solution.

Given \(y = (\sin^{-1} x)^2 + c\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2 \sin^{-1} x \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\)

So \(\sqrt{1 - x^2}\,\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2 \sin^{-1} x\).

Differentiate again with respect to \(x\):

\(\sqrt{1 - x^2}\,\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} \cdot \dfrac{-x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\)

Multiply throughout by \(\sqrt{1 - x^2}\):

\((1 - x^2)\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} - x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2\)

This is the given differential equation, so \(y = (\sin^{-1} x)^2 + c\) is a solution.

Given \(y = e^{-x} + Ax + B\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -e^{-x} + A\)

Differentiate again:

\(\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = e^{-x}\)

Multiply both sides by \(e^x\):

\(e^x \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = e^x \cdot e^{-x} = 1\)

This is the given differential equation, so \(y = e^{-x} + Ax + B\) is a solution.

Given \(y = x^m\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = m x^{m-1}\)

Differentiate again:

\(\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = m(m-1) x^{m-2}\)

Substitute into the left side of the given equation:

\(x^2 \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} - mx \dfrac{dy}{dx} + my\)

\(= x^2 \cdot m(m-1)x^{m-2} - mx \cdot m x^{m-1} + m x^m\)

\(= m(m-1)x^m - m^2 x^m + m x^m\)

\(= x^m\left[m^2 - m - m^2 + m\right] = x^m \cdot 0 = 0\)

This satisfies the given differential equation, so \(y = x^m\) is a solution.

Given \(y = a + \dfrac{b}{x} = a + b x^{-1}\).

Differentiate with respect to \(x\):

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -b x^{-2} = \dfrac{-b}{x^2}\)

Differentiate again:

\(\dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} = 2b x^{-3} = \dfrac{2b}{x^3}\)

Substitute into the left side of the given equation:

\(x \dfrac{d^2 y}{dx^2} + 2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \cdot \dfrac{2b}{x^3} + 2 \cdot \dfrac{-b}{x^2}\)

\(= \dfrac{2b}{x^2} - \dfrac{2b}{x^2} = 0\)

This satisfies the given differential equation, so \(y = a + \dfrac{b}{x}\) is a solution.

Given \(y = e^{ax}\).

Take logarithm of both sides:

\(\log y = ax\)

Differentiate \(y = e^{ax}\) with respect to \(x\):

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = a e^{ax} = a y\)

So \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x \cdot a y = (ax) y\).

But \(ax = \log y\), hence:

\(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y \log y\)

This is the given differential equation, so \(y = e^{ax}\) is a solution.

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 + y^2}{1 + x^2}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{dy}{1 + y^2} = \dfrac{dx}{1 + x^2}\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int \dfrac{dy}{1 + y^2} = \int \dfrac{dx}{1 + x^2}\)

\(\tan^{-1} y = \tan^{-1} x + c\)

This is the general solution.

\(\log\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = 2x + 3y\)

Remove the logarithm:

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{2x + 3y} = e^{2x} \cdot e^{3y}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{dy}{e^{3y}} = e^{2x}\,dx\)

\(e^{-3y}\,dy = e^{2x}\,dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int e^{-3y}\,dy = \int e^{2x}\,dx\)

\(\dfrac{e^{-3y}}{-3} = \dfrac{e^{2x}}{2} + c_1\)

Multiply throughout by \(6\) and rearrange:

\(-2 e^{-3y} = 3 e^{2x} + c\)

i.e. \(3 e^{2x} + 2 e^{-3y} = c\), where \(c\) is an arbitrary constant. This is the general solution.

\(y - x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\)

So \(x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = y\).

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{dy}{y} = \dfrac{dx}{x}\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int \dfrac{dy}{y} = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}\)

\(\log y = \log x + \log c\)

\(\log y = \log(cx)\)

Therefore \(y = cx\). This is the general solution.

\(\sec^2 x \cdot \tan y \cdot dx + \sec^2 y \cdot \tan x \cdot dy = 0\)

Divide throughout by \(\tan x \cdot \tan y\) to separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan x}\,dx + \dfrac{\sec^2 y}{\tan y}\,dy = 0\)

Integrate both sides. Using \(\int \dfrac{\sec^2 t}{\tan t}\,dt = \log|\tan t|\) (since the numerator is the derivative of the denominator):

\(\log|\tan x| + \log|\tan y| = \log c\)

\(\log|\tan x \cdot \tan y| = \log c\)

Therefore \(\tan x \cdot \tan y = c\). This is the general solution.

\(2 e^{x + 2y}\,dx - 3\,dy = 0\)

Write \(e^{x + 2y} = e^x \cdot e^{2y}\):

\(2 e^x \cdot e^{2y}\,dx = 3\,dy\)

Separate the variables:

\(2 e^x\,dx = \dfrac{3\,dy}{e^{2y}} = 3 e^{-2y}\,dy\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int 2 e^x\,dx = \int 3 e^{-2y}\,dy\)

\(2 e^x = 3 \cdot \dfrac{e^{-2y}}{-2} + c_1\)

\(2 e^x = -\dfrac{3}{2} e^{-2y} + c_1\)

Multiply throughout by \(2\) and rearrange:

\(4 e^x + 3 e^{-2y} = c\), where \(c\) is an arbitrary constant. This is the general solution.

\(\cos x \cdot \cos y \cdot dy - \sin x \cdot \sin y \cdot dx = 0\)

Divide throughout by \(\cos y \cdot \cos x\) to separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{\cos y}{\sin y}\,dy = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\,dx\)

i.e. \(\cot y\,dy = \tan x\,dx\).

Integrate both sides:

\(\int \cot y\,dy = \int \tan x\,dx\)

\(\log|\sin y| = -\log|\cos x| + \log c\)

\(\log|\sin y| + \log|\cos x| = \log c\)

\(\log|\sin y \cdot \cos x| = \log c\)

Therefore \(\sin y \cdot \cos x = c\). This is the general solution.

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -k\), where \(k\) is a constant.

Separate the variables:

\(dy = -k\,dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int dy = -k \int dx\)

\(y = -kx + c\)

This is the general solution.

\(\dfrac{\cos^2 y\,dy}{x} + \dfrac{\cos^2 x\,dx}{y} = 0\)

Multiply throughout by \(xy\) to separate the variables:

\(y \cos^2 y\,dy + x \cos^2 x\,dx = 0\)

Use \(\cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2}\):

\(y \cdot \dfrac{1 + \cos 2y}{2}\,dy + x \cdot \dfrac{1 + \cos 2x}{2}\,dx = 0\)

Multiply by \(2\) and integrate both sides:

\(\int y(1 + \cos 2y)\,dy + \int x(1 + \cos 2x)\,dx = c_1\)

Compute \(\int x(1 + \cos 2x)\,dx = \int x\,dx + \int x \cos 2x\,dx\).

By integration by parts, \(\int x \cos 2x\,dx = \dfrac{x \sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4}\).

So \(\int x(1 + \cos 2x)\,dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{x \sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4}\).

Similarly \(\int y(1 + \cos 2y)\,dy = \dfrac{y^2}{2} + \dfrac{y \sin 2y}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2y}{4}\).

Adding:

\(\dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{y^2}{2} + \dfrac{x \sin 2x}{2} + \dfrac{y \sin 2y}{2} + \dfrac{\cos 2x}{4} + \dfrac{\cos 2y}{4} = c_1\)

Multiply throughout by \(4\):

\(2(x^2 + y^2) + 2(x \sin 2x + y \sin 2y) + \cos 2x + \cos 2y = c\), where \(c\) is an arbitrary constant. This is the general solution.

\(y^3 - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

Collect the \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) terms:

\(y^3 = x^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x^2 + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{dy}{y^3} = \dfrac{dx}{x^2 + 1}\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int y^{-3}\,dy = \int \dfrac{dx}{x^2 + 1}\)

\(\dfrac{y^{-2}}{-2} = \tan^{-1} x + c_1\)

\(-\dfrac{1}{2y^2} = \tan^{-1} x + c_1\)

Multiply throughout by \(-2\):

\(\dfrac{1}{y^2} = -2 \tan^{-1} x + c\), where \(c\) is an arbitrary constant. This is the general solution.

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{x + y} + x^2 e^y\)

Write \(e^{x+y} = e^x \cdot e^y\) and take \(e^y\) common on the right:

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^y(e^x + x^2)\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{dy}{e^y} = (e^x + x^2)\,dx\)

\(e^{-y}\,dy = (e^x + x^2)\,dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int e^{-y}\,dy = \int (e^x + x^2)\,dx\)

\(-e^{-y} = e^x + \dfrac{x^3}{3} + c_1\)

Multiply throughout by \(-1\):

\(e^{-y} = -e^x - \dfrac{x^3}{3} + c\)

Equivalently, \(e^x + e^{-y} + \dfrac{x^3}{3} = c\), where \(c\) is an arbitrary constant. This is the general solution.

\(3 e^x \tan y\,dx + (1 + e^x)\sec^2 y\,dy = 0\)

Divide throughout by \(\tan y \,(1 + e^x)\) to separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{3 e^x}{1 + e^x}\,dx + \dfrac{\sec^2 y}{\tan y}\,dy = 0\)

Integrate both sides. In each term the numerator is the derivative of the denominator:

\(3 \log|1 + e^x| + \log|\tan y| = \log c\)

\(\log(1 + e^x)^3 + \log|\tan y| = \log c\)

\((1 + e^x)^3 \tan y = c\)  ... (general solution)

Apply the condition \(x = 0\), \(y = \pi\). Then \(\tan \pi = 0\), so:

\((1 + e^0)^3 \cdot 0 = c\ \Rightarrow\ c = 0\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\((1 + e^x)^3 \tan y = 0\)

Since \((1 + e^x)^3 \neq 0\), this gives \(\tan y = 0\).

\((x - y^2 x)\,dx - (y + x^2 y)\,dy = 0\)

Factorise each bracket:

\(x(1 - y^2)\,dx - y(1 + x^2)\,dy = 0\)

Divide throughout by \((1 + x^2)(1 - y^2)\) to separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{x}{1 + x^2}\,dx - \dfrac{y}{1 - y^2}\,dy = 0\)

Integrate both sides. Using \(\int \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2}\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\log(1 + x^2)\) and \(\int \dfrac{y}{1 - y^2}\,dy = -\dfrac{1}{2}\log|1 - y^2|\):

\(\dfrac{1}{2}\log(1 + x^2) - \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\log|1 - y^2|\right) = c_1\)

\(\dfrac{1}{2}\log(1 + x^2) + \dfrac{1}{2}\log|1 - y^2| = c_1\)

Multiply by \(2\):

\(\log\left[(1 + x^2)(1 - y^2)\right] = c\)  ... (general solution)

Apply the condition \(x = 2\), \(y = 0\):

\(\log\left[(1 + 4)(1 - 0)\right] = c\ \Rightarrow\ c = \log 5\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\(\log\left[(1 + x^2)(1 - y^2)\right] = \log 5\)

i.e. \((1 + x^2)(1 - y^2) = 5\).

\(y(1 + \log x)\dfrac{dx}{dy} - x \log x = 0\)

Rearrange:

\(y(1 + \log x)\dfrac{dx}{dy} = x \log x\)

Separate the variables (take \(x\)-terms on one side, \(y\)-terms on the other):

\(\dfrac{1 + \log x}{x \log x}\,dx = \dfrac{dy}{y}\)

Integrate both sides.

For the left side put \(t = \log x\), so \(dt = \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx\):

\(\int \dfrac{1 + \log x}{x \log x}\,dx = \int \dfrac{1 + t}{t}\,dt = \int\left(\dfrac{1}{t} + 1\right)dt = \log|t| + t = \log|\log x| + \log x\)

For the right side, \(\int \dfrac{dy}{y} = \log|y|\).

Hence:

\(\log|\log x| + \log x = \log y + c_1\)

Apply the condition \(x = e\), \(y = e^2\). Then \(\log x = \log e = 1\) and \(\log|\log x| = \log 1 = 0\), \(\log y = \log e^2 = 2\):

\(0 + 1 = 2 + c_1\ \Rightarrow\ c_1 = -1\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\(\log|\log x| + \log x = \log y - 1\)

[Textbook answer-key error: the printed answer key gives \((\sin x)(e^y+1)=\sqrt2\); with the given condition the constant is \(1\), so \((e^y+1)\sin x=1\) (below).]

\((e^y + 1)\cos x + e^y \sin x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\)

Rearrange:

\(e^y \sin x \dfrac{dy}{dx} = -(e^y + 1)\cos x\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{e^y}{e^y + 1}\,dy = -\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx = -\cot x\,dx\)

Integrate both sides. On the left the numerator is the derivative of the denominator:

\(\log(e^y + 1) = -\log|\sin x| + \log c\)

\(\log(e^y + 1) + \log|\sin x| = \log c\)

\((e^y + 1)\sin x = c\)  ... (general solution)

Apply the condition \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), \(y = 0\). Then \(\sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(e^0 + 1 = 2\):

\(2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} = c\ \Rightarrow\ c = 1\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\((e^y + 1)\sin x = 1\)

\((x + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 1 = 2 e^{-y}\)

Rearrange:

\((x + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 + 2 e^{-y} = \dfrac{e^y + 2}{e^y}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{e^y}{e^y + 2}\,dy = \dfrac{dx}{x + 1}\)

Integrate both sides. On the left the numerator is the derivative of the denominator:

\(\log(e^y + 2) = \log|x + 1| + \log c\)

\(\log(e^y + 2) = \log\big[c(x + 1)\big]\)

\(e^y + 2 = c(x + 1)\)  ... (general solution)

Apply the condition \(x = 1\), \(y = 0\). Then \(e^0 + 2 = 3\) and \(x + 1 = 2\):

\(3 = c \cdot 2\ \Rightarrow\ c = \dfrac{3}{2}\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\(e^y + 2 = \dfrac{3}{2}(x + 1)\)

i.e. \(2(e^y + 2) = 3(x + 1)\).

\(\cos\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right) = a\), where \(a \in \mathbb{R}\).

Take cosine inverse of both sides:

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos^{-1} a\)

Since \(a\) is a constant, \(\cos^{-1} a\) is also a constant. Separate the variables:

\(dy = (\cos^{-1} a)\,dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(y = (\cos^{-1} a)\,x + c\)  ... (general solution)

Apply the condition \(y(0) = 2\), i.e. \(y = 2\) when \(x = 0\):

\(2 = (\cos^{-1} a)(0) + c\ \Rightarrow\ c = 2\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\(y = x \cos^{-1} a + 2\)

Equivalently, \(\dfrac{y - 2}{x} = \cos^{-1} a\), i.e. \(\cos\left(\dfrac{y - 2}{x}\right) = a\).

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos(x + y)\)

Put \(x + y = u\). Then differentiating, \(1 + \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx} - 1\).

Substitute:

\(\dfrac{du}{dx} - 1 = \cos u\)

\(\dfrac{du}{dx} = 1 + \cos u\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{du}{1 + \cos u} = dx\)

Use \(1 + \cos u = 2\cos^2\dfrac{u}{2}\):

\(\dfrac{du}{2\cos^2\frac{u}{2}} = dx\)

\(\dfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\dfrac{u}{2}\,du = dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{\tan\frac{u}{2}}{\frac{1}{2}} = x + c\)

\(\tan\dfrac{u}{2} = x + c\)

Replace \(u = x + y\):

\(\tan\left(\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right) = x + c\)

This is the general solution.

\((x - y)^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = a^2\)

Put \(x - y = u\). Then \(1 - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 - \dfrac{du}{dx}\).

Substitute:

\(u^2\left(1 - \dfrac{du}{dx}\right) = a^2\)

\(u^2 - u^2 \dfrac{du}{dx} = a^2\)

\(u^2 \dfrac{du}{dx} = u^2 - a^2\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{u^2}{u^2 - a^2}\,du = dx\)

Write \(\dfrac{u^2}{u^2 - a^2} = 1 + \dfrac{a^2}{u^2 - a^2}\):

\(\left(1 + \dfrac{a^2}{u^2 - a^2}\right)du = dx\)

Integrate both sides. Using \(\int \dfrac{du}{u^2 - a^2} = \dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left|\dfrac{u - a}{u + a}\right|\):

\(u + a^2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2a}\log\left|\dfrac{u - a}{u + a}\right| = x + c\)

\(u + \dfrac{a}{2}\log\left|\dfrac{u - a}{u + a}\right| = x + c\)

Replace \(u = x - y\):

\((x - y) + \dfrac{a}{2}\log\left|\dfrac{x - y - a}{x - y + a}\right| = x + c\)

Simplify by cancelling \(x\):

\(-y + \dfrac{a}{2}\log\left|\dfrac{x - y - a}{x - y + a}\right| = c\)

This is the general solution.

\(x + y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \sec(x^2 + y^2)\)

Put \(x^2 + y^2 = u\). Then differentiating with respect to \(x\):

\(2x + 2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}\)

so \(x + y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{du}{dx}\).

Substitute into the given equation:

\(\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{du}{dx} = \sec u\)

\(\dfrac{du}{dx} = 2 \sec u\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{du}{\sec u} = 2\,dx\)

\(\cos u\,du = 2\,dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\sin u = 2x + c\)

Replace \(u = x^2 + y^2\):

\(\sin(x^2 + y^2) = 2x + c\)

This is the general solution.

\(\cos^2(x - 2y) = 1 - 2\dfrac{dy}{dx}\)

Put \(x - 2y = u\). Then \(1 - 2\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}\).

So the given equation becomes:

\(\cos^2 u = \dfrac{du}{dx}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{du}{\cos^2 u} = dx\)

\(\sec^2 u\,du = dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\tan u = x + c\)

Replace \(u = x - 2y\):

\(\tan(x - 2y) = x + c\)

This is the general solution.

\((2x - 2y + 3)\,dx - (x - y + 1)\,dy = 0\)

Rewrite as:

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2x - 2y + 3}{x - y + 1} = \dfrac{2(x - y) + 3}{(x - y) + 1}\)

Put \(x - y = u\). Then \(1 - \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx}\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1 - \dfrac{du}{dx}\).

Substitute:

\(1 - \dfrac{du}{dx} = \dfrac{2u + 3}{u + 1}\)

\(\dfrac{du}{dx} = 1 - \dfrac{2u + 3}{u + 1} = \dfrac{(u + 1) - (2u + 3)}{u + 1} = \dfrac{-u - 2}{u + 1}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{u + 1}{-(u + 2)}\,du = dx\)

\(\dfrac{u + 1}{u + 2}\,du = -dx\)

Write \(\dfrac{u + 1}{u + 2} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{u + 2}\):

\(\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{u + 2}\right)du = -dx\)

Integrate both sides:

\(u - \log|u + 2| = -x + c_1\)

Replace \(u = x - y\):

\((x - y) - \log|x - y + 2| = -x + c_1\)

\(2x - y - \log|x - y + 2| = c_1\)  ... (general solution)

Apply the condition \(x = 0\), \(y = 1\):

\(2(0) - 1 - \log|0 - 1 + 2| = c_1\)

\(-1 - \log 1 = c_1\ \Rightarrow\ c_1 = -1\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\(2x - y - \log|x - y + 2| = -1\)

\(x \sin\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) dy = \left[y \sin\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) - x\right] dx\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y \sin\left(\frac{y}{x}\right) - x}{x \sin\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}\)

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\) and \(\dfrac{y}{x} = v\):

\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{vx \sin v - x}{x \sin v} = \dfrac{v \sin v - 1}{\sin v}\)

\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v - \dfrac{1}{\sin v}\)

\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\dfrac{1}{\sin v}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\sin v\,dv = -\dfrac{dx}{x}\)

Integrate both sides:

\(-\cos v = -\log|x| + c_1\)

\(\cos v = \log|x| - c_1\)

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\) and write \(-c_1 = \log c\):

\(\cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \log|x| + \log c = \log|cx|\)

Therefore \(\cos\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \log|cx|\). This is the general solution.

The equation \(xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^2 + 2y^2\) is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\).

Then \(xy\dfrac{dy}{dx} = x(vx)\left(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right) = v^2x^2 + vx^3\dfrac{dv}{dx}\), and \(x^2 + 2y^2 = x^2(1 + 2v^2)\).

So \(v^2x^2 + vx^3\dfrac{dv}{dx} = x^2(1 + 2v^2)\). Divide by \(x^2\): \(v^2 + vx\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + 2v^2\), i.e. \(vx\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + v^2\).

Separate: \(\dfrac{v}{1 + v^2}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\).

Integrate: \(\dfrac12\log(1 + v^2) = \log|x| + c_1\), so \(\log(1 + v^2) = 2\log|x| + 2c_1\), giving \(1 + v^2 = kx^2\).

Since \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\): \(1 + \dfrac{y^2}{x^2} = kx^2\), i.e. \(\dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{x^2} = kx^2\), so \(x^2 + y^2 = kx^4\).

Apply \(y(1) = 0\): \(1 + 0 = k(1) \Rightarrow k = 1\).

\(\therefore\) the particular solution is \(x^2 + y^2 = x^4\).

\(x\,dy + 2y\,dx = 0\)

Separate the variables. Divide by \(xy\):

\(\dfrac{dy}{y} + 2\dfrac{dx}{x} = 0\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\log|y| + 2\log|x| = \log c\)

\(\log|y| + \log x^2 = \log c\)

\(\log(x^2 y) = \log c\)

\(x^2 y = c\)  ... (general solution)

Apply the condition \(x = 2\), \(y = 1\):

\(2^2 \cdot 1 = c\ \Rightarrow\ c = 4\)

Therefore the particular solution is:

\(x^2 y = 4\)

\(x^2 \dfrac{dy}{dx} = x^2 + xy + y^2\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 + xy + y^2}{x^2}\)

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\):

\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 + x \cdot vx + v^2 x^2}{x^2} = 1 + v + v^2\)

\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + v + v^2 - v = 1 + v^2\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{dv}{1 + v^2} = \dfrac{dx}{x}\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\tan^{-1} v = \log|x| + c\)

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\):

\(\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{y}{x}\right) = \log|x| + c\)

This is the general solution.

\((9x + 5y)\,dy + (15x + 11y)\,dx = 0\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{15x + 11y}{9x + 5y}\)

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\):

\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\dfrac{15x + 11vx}{9x + 5vx} = -\dfrac{15 + 11v}{9 + 5v}\)

\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\dfrac{15 + 11v}{9 + 5v} - v = \dfrac{-(15 + 11v) - v(9 + 5v)}{9 + 5v}\)

\(= \dfrac{-15 - 11v - 9v - 5v^2}{9 + 5v} = \dfrac{-5v^2 - 20v - 15}{9 + 5v} = \dfrac{-5(v^2 + 4v + 3)}{9 + 5v}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{9 + 5v}{v^2 + 4v + 3}\,dv = -5\dfrac{dx}{x}\)

Factorise \(v^2 + 4v + 3 = (v + 1)(v + 3)\) and use partial fractions:

\(\dfrac{9 + 5v}{(v + 1)(v + 3)} = \dfrac{A}{v + 1} + \dfrac{B}{v + 3}\)

Then \(9 + 5v = A(v + 3) + B(v + 1)\).
Put \(v = -1\): \(4 = 2A \Rightarrow A = 2\).
Put \(v = -3\): \(-6 = -2B \Rightarrow B = 3\).

So:

\(\int\left(\dfrac{2}{v + 1} + \dfrac{3}{v + 3}\right)dv = -5\int\dfrac{dx}{x}\)

\(2\log|v + 1| + 3\log|v + 3| = -5\log|x| + \log c\)

\(\log\big[(v + 1)^2 (v + 3)^3\big] = \log\dfrac{c}{x^5}\)

\((v + 1)^2 (v + 3)^3 = \dfrac{c}{x^5}\)

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\): \(v + 1 = \dfrac{x + y}{x}\), \(v + 3 = \dfrac{3x + y}{x}\):

\(\left(\dfrac{x + y}{x}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{3x + y}{x}\right)^3 = \dfrac{c}{x^5}\)

\(\dfrac{(x + y)^2 (3x + y)^3}{x^5} = \dfrac{c}{x^5}\)

Therefore \((x + y)^2 (3x + y)^3 = c\). This is the general solution.

\((x^2 + 3xy + y^2)\,dx - x^2\,dy = 0\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 + 3xy + y^2}{x^2}\)

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\):

\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 + 3x \cdot vx + v^2 x^2}{x^2} = 1 + 3v + v^2\)

\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + 3v + v^2 - v = 1 + 2v + v^2 = (1 + v)^2\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{dv}{(1 + v)^2} = \dfrac{dx}{x}\)

Integrate both sides:

\(\int (1 + v)^{-2}\,dv = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}\)

\(\dfrac{(1 + v)^{-1}}{-1} = \log|x| + c_1\)

\(-\dfrac{1}{1 + v} = \log|x| + c_1\)

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\), so \(1 + v = \dfrac{x + y}{x}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{1 + v} = \dfrac{x}{x + y}\):

\(-\dfrac{x}{x + y} = \log|x| + c_1\)

Writing \(c = -c_1\):

\(\dfrac{x}{x + y} = c - \log|x|\)

This is the general solution.

\((x^2 + y^2)\,dx - 2xy\,dy = 0\)

\(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{2xy}\)

This is homogeneous. Put \(y = vx\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx}\):

\(v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{x^2 + v^2 x^2}{2x \cdot vx} = \dfrac{1 + v^2}{2v}\)

\(x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1 + v^2}{2v} - v = \dfrac{1 + v^2 - 2v^2}{2v} = \dfrac{1 - v^2}{2v}\)

Separate the variables:

\(\dfrac{2v}{1 - v^2}\,dv = \dfrac{dx}{x}\)

Integrate both sides. On the left, the numerator is the negative of the derivative of the denominator, so \(\int \dfrac{2v}{1 - v^2}\,dv = -\log|1 - v^2|\):

\(-\log|1 - v^2| = \log|x| + \log c_1\)

\(\log|1 - v^2| = -\log|x| - \log c_1 = \log\dfrac{1}{c_1 x}\)

\(1 - v^2 = \dfrac{c}{x}\)  (writing \(c = \tfrac{1}{c_1}\))

Replace \(v = \dfrac{y}{x}\), so \(1 - v^2 = \dfrac{x^2 - y^2}{x^2}\):

\(\dfrac{x^2 - y^2}{x^2} = \dfrac{c}{x}\)

Multiply throughout by \(x^2\):

\(x^2 - y^2 = cx\)

This is the general solution.
